caption: Is the current drawdown unusual, how much sharper could it get if you buy now, and what dividend yield do you lock in? Drawdown/percentile on price; forward returns on total return; EVT tail for the rare further-fall. Small samples carry wide error bars — episode counts are shown so you can judge.

legend.title: How to read this tab — the two-number convention & columns
legend.body:
Why two numbers everywhere? Every dip stat is conditioned on the asset's own volatility regime today (calm 🟢 vs stressed 🟠 tape). The main number is the history that matches today's regime; the number in (parentheses) is the all-regime reference — shown only when it differs (so an unchanged value isn't repeated). When today's regime has too few comparable dips, the row falls back to all-regime history and says so.

The forward-return table — every cell is a total return measured from your buy price, at that horizon (not a drawdown to the low along the way):

  • If You Hold — how long you hold after buying a dip at least this deep.
  • Typical Median Forward Return — the median outcome at that horizon.
  • Chance You're Still Down — how often you'd be below your buy price at the horizon.
  • If Still Down, Median Loss — among only the times it ended lower, the median loss.
  • 10th-percentile loss — the worst 1-in-10 outcome; 90% of the time the loss is smaller than this.
  • Worst Case Ever — the worst that horizon ever ended (not its lowest point along the way — the further-fall line below each table covers the path).
  • History (Days) — how many comparable days are behind the row.

Verdict callout (top of each card) — a plain read of the reward/risk edge: 🟢 strong buy, 🟡 buy, 🔴 don't buy, ⚪ no signal/not enough data. It uses the Omega ratio (upside dollars per dollar of downside at 12 months; above 1 is favorable), compares it to the asset's normal Omega (the edge), and resamples history for a confidence interval — so a verdict is only “strong buy” when the edge holds up statistically, and says “not enough data” when there are too few comparable dips.

  • Time underwater — after buying a dip this deep, how long it historically took to get back to your buy price (break-even).

This tab is only informative when the dip is deep. A shallow dip (a low “Deeper than …%”) makes the comparison set ≈ all days, so the table ≈ the ticker's ordinary forward returns. The buy-the-dip edge appears when “Deeper than” is high.

verdict.text: 🟢 Strong buy. After dips this deep, SPY had no losing 12-month outcomes in-sample, and this depth ranks in SPY's top third for reward-to-risk. Caveat: in-sample history, not a forecast. Thin history: this call rests on only 2 years of SPY data — the walk-forward test demonstrated this verdict's edge only on 10+ years of history (at 5 years it found none), so treat it as untested rather than trusted.
